en: Hetuduka, Atītattika (The Dyad on Roots, the Triad on the Past)

A past state that is a root-cause (hetu) is a condition, by way of the object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya), for a state that is neither a root-cause nor past. There are nine [instances] in the case of the object-condition; nine in the case of the predominance-condition (adhipati); nine in the case of the proximity-condition (anantara) ... pe ... nine in the case of the decisive support-condition (upanissaya) ... pe ... nine in the case of the disappearance-condition (vigata).

A future state that is a root-cause is a condition, by way of the object-condition, for a state that is neither a root-cause nor future. There are nine [instances] in the case of the object-condition; nine in the case of the predominance-condition and the decisive support-condition (upanissaya).
